title: Build a CoSchedule alternative with Claude: free content calendar spec, 27/27 checks passed
description:
Claude built a CoSchedule alternative from one Markdown spec: all 27 acceptance checks passed in a real browser, along with 63 automated tests.
The test build also exposed 8 gaps in the spec, and every one is now fixed.

We gave Claude one Markdown spec for a small-team content calendar and had it build the tool in four phases: the foundation with channels, campaigns and settings; pieces, the calendar, the backlog and the pipeline; review and publishing; and reminders, overdue flags, the weekly digest and campaign moves. The core rule: a piece only reaches Scheduled through an editor's approval, and nobody approves their own piece. The gaps included sign-in that told strangers to ask an editor to add them when no screen managed people, a spec that let editors withdraw any piece in one section and only the owner in another, and a daily job at 08:00 team time that can't be one UTC cron schedule. What passed, what broke, what we didn't test, and when CoSchedule is still worth paying for.
